04 — How a build runs

We learn your
process before
we write any

01

Sit in the operation

Days 1–3

A shift with your staff, mapping what actually happens — the notebook, the group chat, the workaround everyone knows about. That map is the spec.

02

Design the front, model the data

Week 1–2

Presets that fit go in; the rest is designed to your map. A booking on the site and one at the counter are the same record.

03

Build and pilot live

Week 2–4

A working build in week two, run alongside your current process on real transactions. What doesn't fit gets changed.

04

Hand over, then stay on

Week 4 onward

Training in two sessions. After launch we keep adapting it — new season, new branch, new rule.

08 — Questions

The ones
we always get

Do I have to take the agents?
No. The website and the system are the product and they work fully on their own — installation plus maintenance, nothing else. Specialists are a per-agent add-on you switch on later, if and when the operation is running clean.
How much of it is actually custom?
Typically half. Presets cover the plumbing every business shares — accounts, payments, records, hosting — so budget goes to what's specific to you. If a build turns out 90% preset, we'll say so and quote it lower.
What do the agents cost, and can I start with one?
₱7,999/month for your first specialist, ₱6,499 each for the second and third, ₱4,999 each after that, or ₱29,999 for all six. That sits on top of your maintenance monthly. Almost everyone starts with one — usually Echo on enquiries or Hora on bookings — and adds the next once they stop checking its work.
What happens when the internet goes down?
Counter tools keep working offline and queue locally; the queue syncs and reconciles when the connection returns. Standard on every build, not an upgrade.
Is the receipting actually BIR-compliant?
Yes — correct series, sequence and void trail for your registration type. Set up with your bookkeeper during the build so what the system prints matches what gets filed.
Who owns the code and the data?
You do. The repository and the database are yours, and we'll hand over both on request. The monthly buys hosting, support and changes — not hostage-keeping.
How small is too small?
If you're running one counter and the notebook still works, wait. Where this pays for itself is a second branch, a second shift, or the point where you stop being physically present for every transaction.
